project.source_note: This charter distinguishes the Genesis project from the KORDEX reliability-intelligence system implemented within it. It separates current implementation from planned capabilities; roadmap items are not current capabilities unless implemented and independently verified.

mission: Build a trustworthy reliability-intelligence layer that turns operational observations into traceable evidence, uncertainty-aware assessments, investigations, recommendations, and reusable knowledge for engineers responsible for physical systems.

current_focus.product_positioning: Genesis is the overall engineering project; KORDEX is its reliability-intelligence system.
current_focus.near_term_goal: Strengthen evidence quality, provenance, conflict handling, investigation, and real-telemetry validation while preserving the current architecture.
current_focus.operating_mode: Recorded/offline and local-session workflows first; any device integration remains read-only unless a separately governed future capability is explicitly implemented.

principles.name: Evidence before conclusion
principles.rule: A detected anomaly is not automatically a failure, diagnosis, or cause.

principles.name: Uncertainty triggers investigation
principles.rule: Missing, degraded, conflicting, or untrusted evidence must limit conclusions rather than produce fabricated confidence.

principles.name: Keep epistemic stages separate
principles.rule: Distinguish observation, evidence, inference, reliability state, recommendation, human action, and outcome.

principles.name: Preserve provenance
principles.rule: Retain where evidence came from, what was transformed, what is unknown, and what limitations apply.

principles.name: Memory is not automatic truth
principles.rule: Keep observations and hypotheses distinct from validated or refuted findings.

principles.name: Human-supervised operations
principles.rule: Recommendations are advisory; no automatic robot control is implied by this project context.

principles.name: Heterogeneous by design
principles.rule: Adapters may translate vendor/source payloads, but must not invent reliability conclusions.

flow.name: Sources and adapters
flow.details: Robot/simulator/ROS 2-like payloads; source-specific translation and metadata.

flow.name: Normalization and history
flow.details: Canonical telemetry, unit/field normalization, per-robot history, shared feature contract.

flow.name: Analysis and evidence producers
flow.details: Observation quality, telemetry patterns, engineering signals, optional model inference, diagnosis and risk outputs.

flow.name: Context and memory
flow.details: Historical comparison, fleet context, recurrence context, reliability memory.

flow.name: Decision pipeline
flow.details: Coordinates reliability fusion/state, recommendations, incident lifecycle and evidence synthesis.

flow.name: Evidence and explanation
flow.details: Structured evidence, timeline, provenance, conflicts, limitations and investigation result.

flow.name: KORDEX interface/API
flow.details: Presents returned results, session history, incidents, recommendations and audit records for human review.

offline_path: Shared feature contract and feature engineering
boundaries: Adapters ingest and normalize; they do not own reliability policy.
Telemetry patterns describe behavior; they do not independently prove cause or failure.
Fleet comparison and historical memory are context, not proof.
Offline simulator labels and training-only fields must not become runtime inference inputs.
Project-level goals and roadmap guide development but must not be treated as evidence about an individual robot.

roadmap.name: Consolidate the foundation
roadmap.goal: Preserve the current architecture and make evidence contracts, boundaries, and outputs understandable.

roadmap.name: Evidence hardening
roadmap.goal: Improve evidence independence, provenance, conflict reasoning, observation quality, and anomaly visibility.

roadmap.name: Reliability and investigation lifecycle
roadmap.goal: Improve recovery, hysteresis, reconfirmation, investigation planning, and reassessment.

roadmap.name: Real-world validation
roadmap.goal: Evaluate recorded real telemetry in read-only mode; measure false positives, missed events, and investigation usefulness.

roadmap.name: Durable memory and retrieval
roadmap.goal: Introduce durable storage and historical-case retrieval after memory contracts are stable.

roadmap.name: Field intelligence
roadmap.goal: Add carefully scoped live telemetry ingestion while maintaining read-only boundaries initially.

roadmap.name: Human decision workflows
roadmap.goal: Capture reviewed recommendations, human actions, and outcomes so validated experience can improve future investigations.

roadmap.name: Controlled action interfaces
roadmap.goal: Consider secure, bounded execution only after evidence, safety, identity, authorization, and governance requirements are met.

capabilities: Continuous reliability monitoring across heterogeneous fleets
Multimodal evidence from telemetry, events, maintenance records, diagnostics and eventually visual evidence
Durable reliability memory based on validated findings and outcomes
Human-supervised recommendations and carefully governed future action workflows
Stronger causal and counterfactual analysis only as supporting evidence justifies it
potential_domains: Other complex physical systems after domain-specific validation

explicit_non_goals_and_limits: KORDEX is not another robot controller or robot operating system.
The current prototype is not a production-ready autonomous control system.
Universal failure prediction or physical causality has not been established.
A successful local test does not prove readiness for live fleet deployment.
Production-grade authentication, cryptography, durable distributed storage, and secure action infrastructure are future work unless separately implemented and verified.
